title: Nonlinear Mixed Effects Estimation for Mixed Laminar/Chaotic Systems: A Global Two-Stage Method Applied to a Bimodal Lorenz-63 Ensemble
content: Population estimation methods in routine use (FOCE-I, SAEM, importance-sampling EM) assume that model predictions vary smoothly with the individual parameters. That makes residuals informative and lets the individual likelihood be approximated locally. Both assumptions fail for chaotic structural models, which matter more and more for oscillatory pharmacodynamic systems such as hormone pulsatility and glucose–insulin dynamics. We present a reproducible two-stage pipeline and test it on an intentionally challenging benchmark: 16 Lorenz-63 subjects with log-normal inter-individual variability (IIV), a bimodal population straddling a bifurcation (8 chaotic, 8 periodic), one observed state, and 20% proportional residual error. Stage 1 replaces residual-based likelihoods with feature matching by the simulated method of moments, using features scaled to each subject’s own oscillation period. It also replaces covariance-based standard errors, which inflated the IIV of the weakly identified parameter σ more than five-fold, with objective-function profiles. The scale of these profiles is calibrated per regime by simulating at the subject’s own estimates. Stage 2 combines the profiles in exact-grid or Gibbs hierarchical posteriors, including a mixture model analogous to NONMEM $MIXTURE. Diagnostics include feature-based, marginal-quantile, and peak-aligned visual predictive checks (VPCs), EBEs with shrinkage, and Lyapunov classification. The method recovered the residual error (0.1992 vs 0.200), mixture fraction (0.500 vs 0.500), σ typical value (10.04 vs 10.12), and β IIV (0.057 vs 0.052), and cut individual-estimate EBE error five-fold with respect to the Stage 1 estimates. The IIV of σ was underestimated (0.017 vs 0.032). Chaotic subjects carry almost no information on σ (93% shrinkage), so this estimate effectively reflects the periodic subpopulation. Peak-aligned VPCs passed in the periodic stratum (9% of points outside the 90% intervals) but not in the chaotic stratum (20%), indicating residual misspecification.
